data.entity_name: Machine Learning for Industrial Manufacturing: A Case Study on Injection Molding Machine Selection Support
data.content:
Machine Learning for Industrial Manufacturing: A Case Study on Injection Molding Machine Selection Support
The article being read, published in DATA 2024 proceedings (LNISO 71, pp. 283–291, Springer Nature Switzerland, 2024). It applies Support Vector Machine and Random Forest to real automotive plastics industry data to support injection molding machine selection, finding that Random Forest outperforms SVM (Accuracy 81%, F1 78%, Precision 85%, Recall 81% vs. SVM Accuracy 67%, F1 66%, Precision 66%, Recall 67%).

Corresponding author of the injection molding machine selection paper, affiliated with the Intelligent Automation and BioMed Genomics Laboratory, FST of Tangier, Abdelmalek Essaadi University.

Support Vector Machine
Classifier that handles non-linear relationships through kernel functions and maximizes class margins. With a linear kernel it achieved 67% accuracy and 66% F1-score. With a polynomial kernel it achieved 52% accuracy and 50% F1-score.<SEP>Machine learning algorithm (SVM) suited to high-dimensional spaces and non-linear relationships via kernel functions; applied in the study and compared with Random Forest.<SEP>Machine learning classification model (SVM) applied to injection molding machine selection, achieving Accuracy 67%, F1 66%, Precision 66%, Recall 67%.<SEP>Classification technique. Reference 12 compares its prediction performance with random forest.

Random Forest
Ensemble method that averages multiple decision trees to reduce overfitting and provide feature importance. Its best configuration (700 estimators, max depth 30, bootstrap enabled) achieved 81% accuracy and 78% F1-score.<SEP>Machine learning algorithm applied in the study to the multicriteria injection machine selection problem.<SEP>Machine learning classification model applied to injection molding machine selection, outperforming SVM with Accuracy 81%, F1 78%, Precision 85%, Recall 81%.<SEP>Classification technique. Reference 12 compares its prediction performance with support vector machine.

Feature Importance
Interpretation technique used to explain the machine learning models' predictions for machine selection.<SEP>Interpretability insight provided by Random Forest. SHAP analysis shows that mold characteristics such as weight, height, length and width are the primary contributors to predictions.

Injection Molding
Manufacturing process using clamping and injection units to inject molten material into a mold under high pressure.<SEP>Industrial process in which plastic is injected into a mold under high pressure, then cooled and solidified; widely used for complex plastic parts in automotive, consumer electronics and medical devices.<SEP>Plastic manufacturing process that is the central application domain of most references (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11).

Injection Molding Machine Selection
Problem of selecting the appropriate injection machine for a given product. It is traditionally solved through theoretical calculations and practical trials, which are time-consuming and costly.<SEP>Problem of selecting the appropriate injection press for a product; few studies apply machine learning to it.<SEP>Problem of selecting the most suitable injection molding machine for a product, traditionally requiring clamping force calculations, mold evaluations and trial runs; time-consuming, costly and expertise-dependent.

Multi-Criteria Decision-Making
Decision framework characterizing the assignment of products to injection molding machines in profitability optimization.

Automotive Plastics Industry Data
Real data from the automotive plastics industry used to train and evaluate the SVM and Random Forest models for machine selection.

data.entity_name: Machine Learning for Industrial Manufacturing: A Case Study
data.content:
Machine Learning for Industrial Manufacturing: A Case Study
Article by F. Tayalati et al. that applies Random Forest and SVM models to help manufacturers select the appropriate injection molding machine for a given product. It finds that Random Forest with 700 estimators, max depth 30 and bootstrapping achieves 81% accuracy, 85% precision, 81% recall and 78% F1-score.<SEP>The article being read, by F. Tayalati et al.; applies Random Forest and Support Vector Machine to select injection molding machines (presses) using data from an automotive workshop in Morocco, followed by correlation and SHAP analyses.<SEP>The article being read. It is a case study applying machine learning to industrial manufacturing. Its future perspectives include adding more models such as deep learning, expanding the dataset, and exploring more hyperparameters. It was funded through the Smart DLSP Project of the AL KHAWARIZMI IA-PROGRAM in Morocco.

F. Tayalati
First author of "Machine Learning for Industrial Manufacturing: A Case Study".<SEP>First author of "Machine Learning for Industrial Manufacturing: A Case Study" (listed as F. Tayalati et al.).<SEP>First author of references 1 and 2, both on machine learning applied to injection molding.

data.entity_name: Ref [8] Multi-Agent System and AHP for Machine Selection
data.content:
Ref [8] Multi-Agent System and AHP for Machine Selection
Cited as [8]; used a multi-agent system and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to select the best machine for manufacturing orders based on quality, time, and cost, identifying five criteria (clamping force, tie bar distances, shot weight, time, and cost); its Multi-Agent System reduced Short Shot defects by 10%, Sink Marks by 5%, and Flashing by 30%.

Ref [9] Fuzzy TOPSIS Machine Selection
Cited as [9]; applied Fuzzy TOPSIS to select among 14 electrical molding machines considering rate of return, risk investment, and environmental impact, aiming to make machine selection more autonomous.

SHAP Analysis
Explainability method used to identify the features most impacting predictions of the best model.

Analytical Hierarchy Process
Multi-criteria decision method (AHP) used for machine selection.

Multi-Agent System
System used together with AHP to select machines for manufacturing orders.

Fuzzy TOPSIS
Fuzzy multi-criteria decision method used to select among electrical molding machines.<SEP>Fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making method. Reference 9 uses it to select an electric molding machine.

TOPSIS
Classical multi-criteria decision method used in machine selection.

Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process
FAHP, combined with Taguchi and TOPSIS to determine moldability index.

Taguchi Method
Experimental design method combined with FAHP and TOPSIS in injection molding.

Correlation Analysis
Analysis used to verify machine behavior; revealed correlations of machine size with mold width (0.98), mold weight (0.79), mold height (0.76), mold length (0.75), and part weight (0.61).<SEP>Statistical analysis technique whose principles are explained in reference 14.

data.entity_name: Accuracy, Recall, Precision and F1 Score
data.content:
Accuracy, Recall, Precision and F1 Score
Performance metrics used to evaluate the machine learning models, based on a confusion matrix.

Automotive Injection Workshop Dataset
Dataset collected from an automotive industry workshop in Morocco covering 104 parts, 104 molds, 5 machines, and 10 material types, with features grouped into Part, Material, Mold, and Machine and machine type (clamping force) as output.

data.entity_name: Few studies apply machine learning to injection press selection
data.content:
Few studies apply machine learning to injection press selection
Finding of the literature review: "Many studies have explored machine selection, but few have used artificial intelligence." and "Secondly, only a few works explore the use of machine learning for optimizing machine selection. The majority of machine learning applications focus on parameter optimization, quality prediction, or process monitoring."

data.entity_name: Machine size correlates strongly with mold dimensions and part weight
data.content:
Machine size correlates strongly with mold dimensions and part weight
Statement made in the text: "The heatmap [15] reveals high correlations between machine size and mold characteristics: 0.79 with mold weight, 0.98 with mold width, 0.76 with mold height, 0.75 with mold length, and 0.61 with part weight."

Heatmap
Visualization used to display correlations between Machine Clamping Force and other features.

Confusion Matrix
Performance assessment tool that compares predicted and actual values in classification tasks, using true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives.<SEP>Structure of true positives, false positives, false negatives, and true negatives used as the basis for the evaluation metrics.

Machine Clamping Force
Machine clamping size measured in kN and recorded as a feature in the dataset. Fig. 4 analyzes its correlation with the other dataset features.<SEP>Output variable of the dataset representing machine size in KN; strongly correlated with mold width (0.98), mold weight (0.79), mold height (0.76), mold length (0.75), and part weight (0.61).

Clamping Unit
Mechanical structure of the injection molding machine that maintains the mold's closure under pressure, with the mold mounted on a fixed platen and a movable platen linked to a hydraulic system.

Injection Unit
Mechanical structure of the injection molding machine that uses a screw mechanism to drive molten material through a heated barrel into the mold under high pressure.

Morocco
Country where the automotive industry workshop that provided the study's dataset is located.

Accuracy
Main evaluation metric, defined as the proportion of correct predictions: (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN).

Precision
Metric measuring the accuracy of positive predictions: TP/(TP+FP).

Recall
Also called sensitivity. Metric giving the proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified: TP/(TP+FN).

F1-Score
Metric defined as the harmonic mean of precision and recall, which balances extreme values.

SHAP
Feature attribution method used to show that mold weight, height, length and width are the primary contributors to Random Forest predictions.<SEP>Local interpretation method for machine learning models. Reference 13 uses it to extract spatial effects.

Hyperparameter Tuning
Process whose importance is emphasized by the large performance differences observed between Random Forest configurations.

Injection Mold Dataset
Moderate-sized dataset of molds and parts with features such as material flow rate, material type and machine clamping force. 83 samples were used for training and 21 for testing.

Deep Learning
Proposed as future work for improving injection machine selection.<SEP>Family of models. The current paper names it as a future addition, and reference 2 uses it through an autoencoder.

Data Availability
Primary limitation of the study, because real-world datasets are difficult to obtain.

Base learner that Random Forest averages over to reduce overfitting and produce robust predictions.

Overfitting
A model failure that Random Forest reduces by averaging multiple decision trees.

Functions that let SVM handle non-linear relationships. The study evaluates linear and polynomial kernels.

Flow Rate

Material Type

Mold Characteristics
Mold weight, height, length and width. SHAP identifies them as the primary contributors to Random Forest predictions, which is consistent with the importance of mold assembly and part geometry in injection molding.
